# Ternuxx

**A Native Termux workstation manager with an optional, explicitly routed Debian PRoot.** The Native core owns boot/recovery, SSH, management and native workloads; Debian remains a separate Linux workload provider.

[বাংলা পরিচিতি](bn/README.md) · [Product vision](docs/PRODUCT-VISION.md) · [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) · [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Documentation index](docs/README.md)

## Status

Ternuxx is in active development. **P4 — existing Debian PRoot integration — is in progress**; P5–P10 are planned. The current gate summary and phase evidence live in [phase status](docs/PHASE-STATUS.md). Runtime claims are limited to the device, route, and workload actually checked.

## Guided install — Native Termux

This single command installs Git if needed, clones the repository, and opens the exact Native package preview:

```sh
pkg install git && git clone https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx.git "$HOME/ternuxx" && cd "$HOME/ternuxx" && ./tx install --preview
```

Read the package and dependency transaction. Apply only the saved plan you reviewed, using the exact command printed by the preview:

```sh
./tx install --yes --plan-id <64-character-preview-id>
```

The install is limited to official Termux repositories and refuses package removals or upgrades. It does not install or replace a Debian rootfs. Install the matching Termux:X11 Android app separately. See [installation guide and limits](docs/INSTALLATION.md).

### Clone an existing checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx.git
cd ternuxx
./tx install --preview
```

Use the same reviewed apply command above if you choose to install the previewed packages. To update later, review the repository changes before pulling, then use `git pull --ff-only`.

### Manual installation

1. Install Termux from one source and install its matching Termux:X11 app if you need a desktop.
2. Enable the official Termux X11 package repository, refresh package indexes, and install Git using your normal Termux package workflow.
3. Clone this repository and run `./tx install --preview`.
4. Review and apply the exact preview ID. Start Native desktop with `./tx start`; inspect first with `./tx doctor` and `./tx info`.
5. Open `./tx tui`, `./tx web`, or `./tx mng center` for management interfaces.

Follow [the full installation guide](docs/INSTALLATION.md) for provider setup, Android app requirements, upgrades, and recovery. No clean-device release is claimed yet.

## First commands

```sh
./tx help                 # command help
./tx doctor               # health checks
./tx info                 # detected runtime capabilities
./tx tui                  # interactive terminal UI
./tx web                  # authenticated local Web UI
./tx mng center           # Native GTK management app
./tx db                   # managed shell in the existing Debian guest
tx pgui                   # guest desktop route, when qualified
```

Use `./tx db` for Ternuxx-managed environment handoff; it is a first-party command, distinct from any legacy bare `db` alias. PRoot actions target only the explicitly selected guest. See [operations and command reference](docs/OPERATIONS.md).

## What it manages

- **Native workstation:** desktop lifecycle, health, service/boot state, backups and recovery.
- **Optional Debian PRoot:** guest discovery, selected application shortcuts, terminal handoff and explicitly targeted setup operations.
- **Remote access:** managed SSH on port 8023, separate from the owner-run development channel on 8022.
- **Management clients:** CLI, TUI, Web and GTK share typed operations; supported actions and remaining parity gaps are in the [capability matrix](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md).
- **Graphics:** capability and draw results are route-specific. See [GPU qualification](docs/testing/GPU-ACCELERATION.md) and [known limits](docs/testing/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md).
